title: Drift vs Knock AI vs Storylane RepX: 2026 Pricing & Fit
summary: Drift vs Knock AI vs Storylane RepX compared: real pricing, the 2026 Drift sunset, a migration plan, and which wins for demo-led conversion.
body_markdown:
If you are running a **Drift vs Knock AI** evaluation in 2026, you are really answering two questions at once: which tool converts more inbound pipeline, and what happens to your stack now that Drift is being sunset. My take, as someone who watches buyer-engagement tools for a living: most of these comparisons argue about chat widgets while the real money leaks somewhere else. It leaks at the handoff between a website visit and a booked, useful demo.


> **Definition:** A buyer-engagement platform is software that detects, qualifies, and routes inbound demand across a website and other channels, so a high-intent visitor reaches a conversation or a demo before they lose interest.


I am Madhav Bhandari, CMO at Storylane. I will keep this even-handed, name where each tool wins, and add the third option the other comparisons skip: Storylane RepX. The thesis is simple. Drift vs Knock AI is not a chat-widget contest, it is a conversion-architecture decision, and the winner is whoever gets a qualified buyer into a live product experience fastest.


## TL;DR: Drift vs Knock AI at a glance


Drift built the conversational-marketing category on session-based live chat and bots, and it is now folding into Salesloft. Knock AI positions itself as the AI-era replacement: intent detection, de-anonymization, and multi-channel, async engagement rather than a single chat window. Both are trying to capture demand at the exact moment buyers say it slips away.


That gap is not theoretical. One buyer described the missing step precisely.


> "The chatbot piece seems a very natural progression... obviously it's just maximizing conversion, particularly if you're getting those website views and they're getting through to the demo. You know, it's kind of the final piece almost before it gets passed that perhaps is missed at the moment."
> - \[CEO, data analytics / SaaS\]


Quick verdict: choose Drift only if you are already inside the Salesloft ecosystem and want continuity. Choose Knock AI if you want an intent-first, multi-channel engagement layer and are comfortable with a younger platform. Choose Storylane RepX if the conversion you actually care about is getting buyers into an interactive demo, not just a chat thread.

Here is the shape of the decision before we go deep. I have added RepX as a third column because the honest answer to "Drift vs Knock AI" for many teams is "neither, if the goal is demo conversion." Read the table as a map of intent, not a scoreboard. Drift optimizes for the moment a visitor is on your page, Knock AI optimizes for identifying and qualifying accounts across channels, and RepX optimizes for getting a qualified buyer into a live product experience.


None of those is objectively better; they are answers to different bottlenecks. If your funnel loses people because anonymous traffic never gets identified, that points one way. If it loses people because a booked demo never turns into a compelling product moment, that points another. ## What is Drift? (2026 status)


Drift more or less invented conversational marketing: put a smart chat window on the website, qualify visitors in the moment, and book meetings without a form. Its core kit is live chat, rule-based chatbots, meeting booking, and account-based routing for target accounts. For years it was the default answer when a demand-gen team wanted to convert traffic into conversations.


The important 2026 context is ownership. Drift was acquired by Salesloft in February 2024 (Salesloft, 2024), and its capabilities are being consolidated into the Salesloft platform rather than sold as a growing standalone product. That matters for a buying decision because you are no longer choosing a fast-moving independent tool, you are choosing a feature set inside someone else's roadmap.


Drift strengths and trade-offs:


- **Strengths:** mature live-chat and routing, deep Salesforce and HubSpot history, strong ABM playbooks, and now native alignment with Salesloft's sales engagement stack.
- **Trade-offs:** the standalone product is winding down, innovation is gated by Salesloft's priorities, and pricing has drifted toward quote-based enterprise deals rather than transparent tiers.


## What is Knock AI?


Knock AI is built for the world Drift was not designed for: buyers who research anonymously, arrive with intent already formed, and expect engagement across more than one channel. Rather than waiting for a visitor to open a chat window, it leans on intent detection and de-anonymization to identify accounts and trigger outreach across the website, email, and messaging. Think of it as an intent-first engagement layer with AI SDR-style follow-up rather than a chat widget.


The buyer instinct behind this model is real. Teams increasingly want to qualify demand before it reaches a rep and to know which accounts touched which assets, which is exactly what intent routing promises. Keep it factual, though: Knock AI is a positioning statement as much as a product, and the intent-first model only pays off if your traffic is high enough to feed reliable signals. On a thin-traffic site, intent scoring gets noisy, and you are back to guessing. Judge it on whether it can identify your specific accounts, not on the category story.

## How each platform works


The mechanism is where this comparison earns its keep, because "AI chat" hides very different architectures. Understanding the flow tells you which tool fits your funnel, and it is the same thinking behind good[digital sales rooms](https://www.storylane.io/blog/digital-sales-room-software) : meet the buyer where their intent already is.


**Drift's session-based flow.** A visitor lands, a bot or live-chat playbook fires based on page and rules, the visitor answers qualifying questions in that session, and the bot books a meeting or routes to a rep. It is reactive and moment-bound: if the visitor does not engage in that session, the opportunity is largely gone.


**Knock AI's intent-detection flow.** The platform identifies the account, scores intent from behavior and third-party signals, and then engages across channels rather than a single window. The qualification happens before a human rep is involved, which is the workflow buyers describe wanting.


> "I want to know what demos have been shown or what people have looked at inside there, or vice versa, what demos are being used against which accounts. How do you support me on that?"
> - \[Partner, sales consultancy\]


That quote is the tell. The buyer is not asking for a prettier chat window, they are asking for attribution and qualification across the whole engagement, which is why intent-first framing beats session-based chat for most modern funnels.

### Meeting routing and integrations


All three route meetings and connect to Salesforce and HubSpot, so integrations rarely break the tie. What breaks the tie is what happens inside the meeting you booked. A routed meeting is only as good as the qualification behind it, which is why I would rather over-invest in the pre-meeting step and the demo than in the calendar mechanics. If your reps still waste the first call on discovery basics, fix how you[structure a discovery call](https://www.storylane.io/blog/discovery-call-agenda) before you blame the routing tool.


## Drift vs Knock AI pricing compared (real numbers)


Pricing is where competitors get lazy or stale, so let me be precise about what is actually known and what is not. Drift no longer publishes clean public tiers; deals are quote-based, enterprise-oriented, and negotiated inside Salesloft agreements. I will not repeat a specific Drift dollar figure here, because the numbers floating around competitor blogs are unverified and post-acquisition pricing is bespoke, so treat any single figure you see elsewhere with suspicion.


Knock AI publishes tiered pricing on its site, and it generally positions as more accessible than legacy enterprise chat, but confirm current rates directly rather than trusting a screenshot in someone's blog. For RepX, RepX Chat has published, visitor-based pricing: Growth at $2,000/month (up to 10,000 monthly visitors), Premium at $3,000/month (up to 40,000), and Enterprise custom, with a 30-day free trial.


Vendor Pricing model What to watch

Knock AI Published tiers (verify current rates) Usage and data-enrichment costs at scale

The honest buyer move is to price the whole motion, not the license. Add implementation, data enrichment, and the SDR hours needed to work the leads any of these tools surface, then compare that fully loaded cost against pipeline. A cheap tool that still needs three SDRs to chase raw intent is not cheap.


## Performance and ROI: what the numbers actually say


Here is where I break from the pack. Vendor landing pages throw around dramatic multipliers, but I will not repeat a competitor's unaudited "6x" stat as if it were fact, because you cannot verify it and neither can I. Instead, let me give you a defensible model you can run with your own inputs, and one grounded external anchor: reps spend only about 40% of their time actually selling (Salesforce, State of Sales, 2026). Every unqualified lead you route eats into that 40%.


Run the math like this, with conservative, stated assumptions:


1. Start with 1,000 inbound website visitors a month who show buying signals.
2. Assume a baseline of 3% booking a demo without strong engagement tooling, so 30 demos.
3. Assume better qualification and routing lifts that to 4.5%, so 45 demos, a modest 1.5-point gain.
4. That is 15 extra demos a month, or 180 a year.
5. At a 20% demo-to-closed-won rate and a $12,000 average deal, that is 36 wins and roughly $432,000 in new revenue a year.


Nothing in that model is magic, and you can dial every assumption to your reality. The point is that the lever is not the chat widget, it is lifting the demo-conversion rate, which is why I obsess over the[micro-conversions on your site](https://www.storylane.io/blog/101-guide-to-micro-conversions) that lead to a booked demo. Move that one number and the ROI takes care of itself.


## Drift is sunsetting: what it means for you


If you are comparing Drift to anything in 2026, the sunset is not a footnote, it is the headline. Competitors get this timeline wrong constantly, so here is the accurate version, sourced.


When What happened


Feb 2024 Salesloft acquired Drift (Salesloft, 2024)


2024 to 2025 Drift capabilities begin consolidating into the Salesloft platform


Dec 2025 Salesloft and Clari merge, creating the Clari + Salesloft entity


Mar 2026 Standalone Drift sunset announced, with functionality folding into the platform (Clari + Salesloft, 2026)


What this means practically: if you buy Drift today, you are buying into Salesloft's roadmap and packaging, not an independent product with its own trajectory. That is fine if you are already a Salesloft shop and want one throat to choke. It is a real risk if you wanted a best-of-breed engagement tool that keeps investing independently. Either way, do not let a vendor scare you into a rushed migration; a sunset gives you a planning window, so use it.


Be skeptical of any comparison that gets this timeline wrong, because several do. Some pages attribute Drift's ownership to a private-equity firm or muddle the dates, and that sloppiness should make you question their pricing and feature claims too. The clean facts are the ones above: a 2024 acquisition by Salesloft, consolidation through 2024 and 2025, and a 2026 sunset of the standalone product. If a vendor cannot get a public, checkable timeline right, do not trust them with your pipeline.


## Migrating from Drift to Knock AI (without losing pipeline)


This is the section every competitor skips or writes only for their own product, so let me make it genuinely useful and vendor-neutral in spirit. The goal is continuity: no dropped conversations, no broken routing, no dark period where inbound leads fall on the floor. Treat it as a project, not a switch you flip.


1. **Inventory your playbooks.** Export every Drift bot flow, routing rule, and qualification question. You cannot rebuild what you have not documented.
2. **Map integrations first.** Confirm the new tool writes to the same Salesforce and HubSpot fields before you move traffic, so reporting does not break.
3. **Run in parallel.** Keep Drift live on a subset of pages while the replacement handles another, and compare booked-meeting rates before cutting over fully.
4. **Protect the demo step.** Whatever captures the lead, make sure it hands off cleanly into the product experience; this is where[automating your product demos](https://www.storylane.io/blog/demo-automation) keeps conversion intact during the switch.
5. **Cut over by segment.** Move your highest-intent pages last, once you trust the new routing on lower-stakes traffic.


Buyers describe exactly why the demo handoff deserves this care.


> "We do see more and more people that just come into the website and book a demo because they probably read about us in ChatGPT or in other places that we can track... but our sales cycle is very long and it can take years."
> - \[Product leader, government / security\]


If demand is arriving self-serve and the cycle is long, every booked demo is precious. A sloppy migration that drops even a handful of them is far more expensive than the license you are trying to save on.


## Where Storylane RepX fits


Full disclosure: this is us. RepX is Storylane's AI agent, and it exists because we kept seeing the same failure in these evaluations: teams optimize the chat and still lose buyers at the demo. RepX qualifies inbound conversations and drives high-intent visitors straight into an interactive demo, so the "final piece" the CEO above described stops getting missed. The mechanism is not a smarter chat window, it is connecting engagement to a live product experience.


We built it partly because of pain buyers kept describing about demo content itself.


> "We have to make a specific demo of a tool for a. For putting it in the website. We can't use any other product that we already did. It's not going to work."
> - \[Product manager, energy tech\]


And the mobile-embedding failure that quietly kills conversion:


> "So what we were trying to do is embed a tour into a WordPress page and when seeing the workplace through a mobile device, the tour didn't auto scale."
> - \[Co-founder / product lead, energy tech\]


Where RepX does not fit: if your buyers never come to your site to explore a product, or you sell a service with no demonstrable interface, an interactive-demo layer is the wrong tool and I will say so plainly. RepX also is not a full replacement for a broad multi-channel intent platform if outbound de-anonymization is your primary need. It shines when the conversion you care about is getting a qualified buyer into a demo, and when you want text-first, non-intrusive AI engagement that stays out of the buyer's way.


## Which should you choose: Drift vs Knock AI vs Storylane RepX?


There is no universal winner, only the right fit for your motion. Here is the honest decision framework.


- **Choose Drift if** you are already committed to Salesloft and value continuity over independent innovation. You will get mature routing inside a stack you already own.
- **Choose Knock AI if** you want an intent-first, multi-channel engagement layer and can accept a younger platform. It fits teams whose problem is identifying and qualifying anonymous demand.
- **Choose Storylane RepX if** your conversion bottleneck is the website-to-demo handoff and you want engagement tied to a real product experience.
- **For enterprise ABM,** weight integrations and routing depth heavily, and make sure whatever you pick strengthens your[ABM funnel](https://www.storylane.io/blog/perfect-abm-funnel) rather than adding another disconnected tool.


The meta-point of this whole Drift vs Knock AI question: do not buy a chat widget when what you actually need is a conversion engine. Decide which number you are trying to move, then buy the tool that moves it.


## FAQ


**Is Drift shutting down, and when?**


Yes. Following Salesloft's 2024 acquisition, the standalone Drift sunset was announced in March 2026 (Clari + Salesloft, 2026), with its capabilities folding into the platform. If you are buying today, you are effectively buying into Salesloft's roadmap rather than an independent Drift product.


**What is the best Drift alternative in 2026?**


It depends on the job. If you need intent-first multi-channel engagement, Knock AI is a strong candidate; if your bottleneck is converting visitors into interactive demos, Storylane RepX is the better fit. Choose based on the conversion step you are trying to improve, not on brand familiarity.


**How much does Drift cost vs Knock AI?**


Drift is quote-based and enterprise-oriented, with bespoke pricing now negotiated within Salesloft agreements rather than a public rate card. Knock AI publishes tiered pricing that generally positions as more accessible, but confirm current rates directly. Always price the full motion, including implementation and SDR time, not just the license.


**What is the difference between Drift's chatbot and Knock AI's intent detection?**


Drift's model is session-based: it engages a visitor in the moment through a chat playbook. Knock AI's model is intent-based: it identifies and scores accounts, then engages across multiple channels before a rep is involved. Session-based chat is reactive, intent detection is proactive.


**Can I migrate my Drift playbooks and routing to Knock AI?**


Yes, with planning. Export your bot flows and routing rules, map integrations to the same CRM fields, run both tools in parallel on different traffic, and cut over by segment starting with lower-intent pages. The goal is zero dropped conversations during the transition.
